architecture: standardise((features - xm) / xs) -> Linear(1920, 512) -> GELU (erf) -> Dropout(0.2) -> Linear(512, 256) -> GELU (erf) -> Linear(256, 22): 11 standardised means and 11 log-variances (clamped to [-6, 4])
output: per frame: mean and standard deviation of each target, a lab scan's pixel L* percentiles, L75 - L25, L90 - L10 and chroma at network size

training.corpus: FilmCorpus lab scans, 8 stocks (ektar100, gold200, portra, portra160, portra400, portra800, pro160ns, pro400h)
training.split: by photographer: pool C = sha1(photographer) mod 100 < 10 (held out, both sites); pool A = the remaining photohito photographers; pool B = the remaining flickr photographers
training.input: frozen DINOv3 features of the clean scan (15 % of draws) or of one of 4 randomly perturbed copies (exposure, gamma, contrast, black and white points, saturation, a*/b* cast), at network size
training.loss: Gaussian negative log-likelihood on standardised targets
training.early_stopping: 5 % of pool A's photographers held out; best epoch by mean absolute error over the perturbed copies
training.source: whitelab TONE arm: tools/extract_corpus.py --K 4, tools/train_heads.py A --kind pool

validation_pool_C.note: mean absolute error over the perturbed copies, in L* (C* for Cmean): head / corpus mean / the perturbed input's own value

tone_head.bin.format: TNH1: uint32 in_dim, hidden1, hidden2, targets; float32 xm, xs, w1, b1, w2, b2, w3, b3, ym, ys (little-endian)
